pool.text: The name Beijing was applied to the city during the Ming dynasty.
The Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception was built as the oldest Catholic church.
Beijing was declared the sole capital of the empire.
The Yonghe Temple was decreed to serve as a research facility and residence.
Anglo-French forces captured the outskirts of the city, looting and burning the Old Summer Palace.
The capital was formally moved to Nanjing following the success of the Northern Expedition.
Beijing fell to Japan and was made the seat of the Provisional Government.
The People's Liberation Army seized control of the city peacefully during the campaign.
The Beijing railway station opened as one of the city's main railway stations.
The Beijing Subway began operating and now has numerous lines and stations.
The first rock band in Beijing named Peking All-Stars was formed.
The urban area of Beijing expanded greatly with the completion of the 2nd Ring Road.
Père David's deer was reintroduced to Beijing after becoming extinct in China.
Beijing Airport Economic Zone was created surrounding the capital airport.
The Beijing West railway station opened as a main transportation hub.
The Beijing barbastelle bat species was discovered in caves of Fangshan District.
One dust storm dumped nearly 50,000 tons of dust onto the city.
The city hosted the Summer Olympics and Summer Paralympics Games.
The Beijing–Tianjin intercity railway opened as a high-speed rail line.
Chongwen and Xuanwu were merged into Dongcheng and Xicheng, respectively.
